speaker: Jiarong Wu
affiliation: Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, New York, USA
bio: Jiarong Wu obtained her bachelor's degree in engineering from Tsinghua University in 2014, then pursued her Ph.D. in mechanical engineering with Prof. Luc Deike at Princeton University on ocean surface wave dynamics using high-fidelity numerical simulations. Since September 2023, she has worked as a postdoctoral research associate with Prof. Laure Zanna at the Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences. Her postdoctoral work centers around parameterization of air-sea interaction in weather and climate models, as part of the multi-institutional project LEAP.
talkTitle: Air-sea flux parameterization: a data-driven approach and its online realization
abstract: Accurately quantifying air-sea fluxes is important for understanding air-sea interactions and improving coupled weather and climate systems. This study introduces a probabilistic framework to represent the uncertain nature of air-sea fluxes. Assuming Gaussian distributions conditioned on the input variables, neural networks and eddy-covariance measurement data are used to estimate the mean and variance of the fluxes by minimizing negative log-likelihood loss. The trained networks provide alternative mean flux estimates to existing bulk algorithms and quantify the uncertainty around them, and stochastic parameterizations can be constructed by sampling from the predicted distributions. Test results in a single-column forced ocean model and in a coupled CESM historical configuration will be discussed.
